infinite-scroll-list.promptSeed:
Build an infinite scroll list with an intersection sentinel:

### InfiniteList({ items = [], onLoadMore, hasMore, loading }: { items?: string[]; onLoadMore: () => void; hasMore: boolean; loading: boolean }): JSX.Element:
- Render `items` in a list (`<ul>` with one `<li>` per item) followed by a sentinel element observed with an `IntersectionObserver`.
- The sentinel is `<li ref={sentinelRef} data-sentinel aria-hidden="true" />`.
- When the sentinel intersects (becomes visible), call `onLoadMore()`.
- Do not call `onLoadMore()` while `loading` is `true`.
- When `hasMore` is `false`, stop loading and disconnect the observer.

Build an accessible star rating as a controlled component:

```ts
interface StarRatingProps {
  value?: number;
  max?: number;
  onChange?: (rating: number) => void;
}
```

### StarRating({ value = 0, onChange, max = 5 }: StarRatingProps): JSX.Element
- **DOM Structure**: Render `<div role="radiogroup" aria-label="Rating">` containing `max` `<button type="button" role="radio">` star buttons rendering the `★` character.
- **ARIA & Labels**: Each button has `aria-label="1 star"`, `"2 stars"`, ..., and `aria-checked={true}` only for the star matching `value`.
- **Roving `tabIndex`**: Only the selected star (or the first star when `value` is 0) has `tabIndex={0}`; all others have `tabIndex={-1}`.
- **Visual State**: Stars up to the displayed rating carry `data-filled="true"` (others `"false"`). Hovering over a star previews that rating until the pointer leaves the group.
- **Selection**: Clicking star `n` calls `onChange(n)`. Clicking the **CURRENT** rating calls `onChange(0)`.
- **Keyboard Navigation**:
  - `ArrowRight` / `ArrowUp` call `onChange(min(max, value + 1))`.
  - `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowDown` call `onChange(max(1, value - 1))`.

#### Optional Styling (CSS is not graded)
Optional helper classes are available in the preview environment:
- `.star-rating`: horizontal flex container with star spacing.
- `.star-btn`: clean button styling without borders, smooth hover scale, and golden amber color when `[data-filled="true"]`.
You may use these classes, custom styles, or your own class names.

Build an accessible dropdown menu component:

### DropdownMenu({ label, items, onSelect }: { label: string; items: MenuItem[]; onSelect: (id: string) => void }): JSX.Element:
- `items` is an array of `MenuItem` (`[{ id, label, disabled? }]`).

- **Menu**: While open, render `<ul role="menu">` with `<li role="menuitem" tabIndex={-1}>` items (disabled ones get `aria-disabled="true"`).

  - Selecting (by click or key) calls `onSelect(id)`, closes the menu, and returns focus to the trigger (disabled items cannot be selected).
  - `Escape` closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.
  - A `mousedown` outside the component or pressing `Tab` closes the menu.

live-announcer.promptSeed:
```ts
interface AnnounceOptions {
  politeness?: 'polite' | 'assertive';
}

type AnnounceFn = (message: string, options?: AnnounceOptions) => void;
```

Build a screen reader announcer system consisting of `AnnouncerProvider` and `useAnnounce()`.

### AnnouncerProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }): JSX.Element:
- **DOM Structure**: Renders `children` followed by two live regions:
  - Polite region: `<div role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">`
  - Assertive region: `<div role="alert" aria-live="assertive" aria-atomic="true">`
- **Visual Hiding**: Hide both regions visually while keeping them accessible to screen readers (e.g. `position: absolute`, `width: 1px`, `height: 1px`, `overflow: hidden`, `clip`). Never use `display: none`, `visibility: hidden`, or the `hidden` attribute, which would silence assistive technology.

### useAnnounce(): AnnounceFn:
- **Returns**: `announce(message, { politeness = 'polite' } = {})`.
- **Targeting**:
  - `announce(message)` (or `{ politeness: 'polite' }`): Sets `message` in the polite region and empties the assertive region.
  - `announce(message, { politeness: 'assertive' })`: Sets `message` in the assertive region and empties the polite region.
- **Repeat Handling**: Screen readers only speak text that **changes**. To ensure repeating the same message speaks every time, toggle a trailing non-breaking space (`'\u00a0'`): e.g. `'Saved'`, `'Saved\u00a0'`, `'Saved'`.
- **Identity**: `announce` must maintain a stable function identity across renders (`useCallback`).

    - `aria-label={label}`
  - Option attributes:
    - `id={option.id}`
    - `role="option"`
    - `aria-selected={index === activeIndex}`
    - `aria-disabled={option.disabled || undefined}`
- **Live Status Announcements**:
  - Includes an element with `role="status"` and `aria-live="polite"`:
    - When open with options: announces `"{count} results available"`.
    - When query is entered but matches 0 options: announces `"No results found"`.
    - Otherwise empty when closed or before interaction.
- **Filtering**:
  - Filters `options` case-insensitively by matching `option.label.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase())`.
  - When typing, opens the listbox if there are matching results.
- **Keyboard Navigation**:
  - `ArrowDown`:
    - If closed, opens the listbox and sets active descendant to the first enabled option.
    - If open, moves active descendant to the next enabled option (wrapping around).
  - `ArrowUp`:
    - If closed, opens the listbox and sets active descendant to the last enabled option.
    - If open, moves active descendant to the previous enabled option (wrapping around).
  - `Enter`:
    - If listbox is open and an enabled option is active, selects it: calls `onSelect(option)`, closes the listbox, and sets the input value to `option.label`.
  - `Escape`:
    - Closes the listbox without selecting.
- **Mouse Interaction**:
  - Clicking an enabled option selects it, calls `onSelect(option)`, closes the listbox, and sets the input value to `option.label`.
  - Clicking a disabled option does nothing.

drag-sortable-list.promptSeed:
Build an accessible drag-and-drop sortable list supporting both pointer drag-and-drop and keyboard/button reordering.

## Description
```ts
export interface SortableItem {
  id: string;
  label: string;
}

export interface DragSortableListProps {
  items: SortableItem[];
  onReorder?: (items: SortableItem[]) => void;
}
```

### DragSortableList({ items, onReorder }: DragSortableListProps): JSX.Element
- **List Rendering**:
  - Renders a list container with `data-sortable-list`.
  - Each item is rendered with `data-item-id={item.id}`, `data-item-index={index}`, and attribute `draggable="true"`.
  - Renders the item's label in `data-item-label`.
- **Keyboard & Button Reordering**:
  - Each item renders a "Move Up" button (`data-action="move-up"`) and a "Move Down" button (`data-action="move-down"`).
  - Move Up is disabled on the first item (`index === 0`).
  - Move Down is disabled on the last item (`index === items.length - 1`).
  - Clicking Move Up swaps the item at `index` with `index - 1`, updates list state, and calls `onReorder(newItems)`.
  - Clicking Move Down swaps the item at `index` with `index + 1`, updates list state, and calls `onReorder(newItems)`.
- **Drag and Drop Interactions**:
  - On `dragstart`, sets data transfer format `'text/plain'` with the source index, and tracks active drag state.
  - On `dragover`, calls `preventDefault()` on the event to allow dropping.
  - On `drop`, calls `preventDefault()`, moves the dragged item from its origin index to the target item's index, updates state, and calls `onReorder(newItems)`.
  - If dropped onto the same index, no reordering occurs.

### Optional Styling (CSS is not graded):
Preloaded helper classes are available if you wish to use them:
- `.sortable-list` (or `[data-sortable-list]`): Resets list style with vertical flex gap.
- `.sortable-item` (or `[data-item-id]`): Card container with grab cursor, border, and button spacing.
